route_definitions.computer_use: Operate a live desktop, browser, or application GUI via screenshots, mouse clicks, keyboard input, or window automation.
route_definitions.visual_analysis: Read-only inspection or comparison of images, screenshots, UI mockups, or design frames without writing UI code or clicking a live GUI.
route_definitions.frontend_implementation: Implement or style UI components, layouts, CSS, React/Vue/Tkinter views, or visual interactions in code.
route_definitions.general_implementation: Implement, modify, or refactor backend, CLI, service, or library code in a repository.
route_definitions.debug_review: Diagnose a bug, race condition, crash, or regression; fix an isolated defect; OR perform a read-only code/diff/release/security review or independent audit.
route_definitions.exploration_analysis: Read-only codebase exploration, dependency mapping, log/telemetry forensics, or architectural tracing.
route_definitions.research_packet: Execute a quantitative experiment, backtest, statistical evaluation, or benchmark script and report metrics.
route_definitions.web_research: Survey public documentation, vendor specs, open-web articles, historical/cultural motifs, or academic literature and synthesize findings (even if the output is saved to a local Markdown path).
route_definitions.text_in_text_out: Draft, translate, polish, or restructure self-contained text, narrative dialogue, documentation, or copy when the needed source material is already in the brief.
route_definitions.self_contained_code: Write or verify a standalone algorithm, data structure, or script whose specification/inputs are self-contained in the brief without needing un-inlined local repository modules.
route_definitions.bounded_bulk_work: Apply a uniform, mechanical transformation or checklist across many files or items.
route_definitions.tool_execution: Run an explicit operational runbook, build/release pipeline, or CLI command sequence.
route_definitions.complex_build_plan: Author a multi-phase engineering specification, system migration plan, or architectural blueprint before implementation.
route_definitions.direction_reasoning: High-depth mathematical proof/derivation, formal critique, or first-principles strategic/architectural paradigm design.

dimension_rubric.anti_inflation_rule: Score ONLY functional work the worker performs, never brief length or Markdown structure. Coordinator headers (`Parent session agent ID`, `工作目录`), role/AGENTS/SKILL docs, communication rules, and output/receipt paths are boilerplate—ignore them for `reasoning_depth`, `code_complexity` and `axis_demand`.
dimension_rubric.local_only_positive_vs_negative: CONTRAST RULE for `local_only`: `true` when depending on un-inlined files/dirs/repos on THIS machine (reading, copying, searching, editing, building, or testing local files) or local processes/daemons/GUI/env. `false` when all required inputs are inlined or from the public web (`web_research`, `self_contained_code`, `text_in_text_out`, `direction_reasoning`, `complex_build_plan`), even if a local output path is named.
dimension_rubric.read_only_review: CONTRAST RULE for `read_only_review`: `true` ONLY for read-only code/PR/diff/branch/security/release reviews or independent audits that write NO repo production/test code (`code_complexity: 0`, `work_kind: debug_review`, even when saving a review report file to a specified path). `false` when fixing issues from a prior review (`Fix the review findings`), implementing/modifying code, diagnosing live runtime/log symptoms without a diff/code audit, or running ops commands.
dimension_rubric.wants_fast: CONTRAST RULE for `wants_fast`: `true` ONLY when affirmatively requesting fast mode, priority tier, urgent/ASAP turnaround, or a pre-reset quota sprint (`pre-reset sprint`, `before quota resets`, `重置前冲刺`) without negation. `false` when negated (`Do NOT use fast mode`, `no rush`, `不用开启fast`), when fast/immediate only describes an in-task runtime step (`click Save immediately`), when merely mentioning quota/reset without requesting fast execution, or when unmentioned.
dimension_rubric.reasoning_depth: `1` (Routine): explicit command/checklist/runbook, trivial config tweak, or mechanical bulk edit; `2` (Standard/Hard): single/multi-module feature, bug diagnosis/fix, read-only PR review, or structured research; `3` (Coupled): cross-module refactor with strict invariants, deep concurrency forensics, or migration plan in an existing system; `4` (Frontier): whole-product/system architecture or detailed game-system/economy/combat math from scratch, ultra-low-latency network design, or formal mathematical proof/critique.
dimension_rubric.multi_task_vs_single_task: `multi_task: true` ONLY when bundling 2+ independent deliverables assignable to separate workers in parallel. Sequential steps (`diagnose -> fix -> test -> report`) or one report covering sub-questions is ONE task (`multi_task: false, task_count: 1`).
dimension_rubric.axis_demand: Level 0..3 per category: how much THIS task needs it. divergence: 0 a known spec or checklist, 1 small judgment calls, 2 several options to compare or a research/data-analysis question to investigate and synthesize, 3 open-ended creative writing, open research synthesis, or a first-principles redesign. coding: 0 no code read or written, 1 a small script or config change or a test-verified result, 2 a production module with its tests or a review/audit of one, 3 coupled modules, concurrency, protocol or core-library work, a whole-system review, or a costly irreversible defect. aesthetics: 0 no visual output, 1 tidy formatting only, 2 a user-facing screen/page/chart/document whose look matters, 3 design-led work (a new interface or interaction, a visual identity, a 3D scene). tool_operation: 0 reads files and runs a few shell commands, 1 routine tool or API calls, 2 heavy tool/API orchestration or the worker itself stays inside a live external system (game, ticket queue, order book, live page or chat) where slow turns hurt, 3 reads images or screenshots inside the loop or operates a GUI. Writing or fixing software about real-time systems is coding, not a live loop.
dimension_rubric.expected_hours: Measured on this host: agents finish a review, investigation, multi-file fix or runbook brief in about 0.3h (middle half 0.2-0.6) and a feature across 8+ files in 1-3h. This overrides the schema's generic hour examples: a multi-file feature or investigation is 0.3-0.6h, not 1-3. Brief length, headings and boilerplate add nothing.

## Specification (Self-Contained)
Write a pure Python 3.11 module `interval_merger.py` with no third-party dependencies that implements:
`merge_weighted_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int, float]], min_gap: int = 0) -> list[tuple[int, int, float]]`

- Intervals are half-open `[start, end)` with `start < end` and positive float weight.
- Overlapping or adjacent intervals within `min_gap` merge into `[min_start, max_end)` with length-weighted average weight.
